evals.prompt: Build the new cursor-pagination API and keep committing as you work without pushing anything. The types, endpoint, and tests can be completed in separate meaningful units.
evals.expected_output: Plans outcome-based checkpoints, verifies each complete unit, commits only explicit paths, records each commit hash, and never runs git push.
assertions: Checkpoint boundaries follow complete outcomes instead of time or file count.
Each commit is verified before work begins on the next checkpoint.
No checkpoint is pushed; progress reports include local commit hashes.

evals.prompt: Refactor the parser and create local checkpoints while you go. Halfway through the rename the project will not compile, but the final parser and regression tests will pass.
evals.expected_output: Does not commit the broken halfway state and waits until the refactor plus required tests form a green, reviewable checkpoint.
assertions: Known-broken intermediate work is not committed.
Dependent rename and consumer changes remain together until the repository is usable.
The completed refactor is labeled with a truthful Conventional Commit.

evals.prompt: Keep making meaningful local commits without pushing during this feature. The branch has an upstream, and the remote advances while you work.
evals.expected_output: Keeps committing locally, notes the upstream drift without pulling, merging, rebasing, or pushing, and reports the unpushed checkpoint sequence at the end.
assertions: The workflow never runs git push, pull, merge, or rebase.
Upstream drift is reported instead of reconciled automatically.
The completion report states which commits remain unpushed.
